proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\kappa_0\in[1/2,1]\).  The definition of \(b_0\) makes it the positive root of
\[
b_0^2-\kappa_0b_0-1=0.
\]
Consequently, using \(a_0=b_0^{-1}\),
\[
a_0b_0=1,
\qquad
b_0-a_0=\kappa_0.
\]
Let \(S\) take the values \(-a_0\) and \(b_0\) with probabilities
\[
p_-:=\frac{b_0}{a_0+b_0},
\qquad
p_+:=\frac{a_0}{a_0+b_0},
\]
respectively.  Direct calculation gives
\[
\mathbb E[S]
=\frac{-a_0b_0+b_0a_0}{a_0+b_0}=0,
\]
\[
\mathbb E[S^2]
=\frac{a_0^2b_0+b_0^2a_0}{a_0+b_0}
=a_0b_0=1,
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E[S^3]
=\frac{-a_0^3b_0+b_0^3a_0}{a_0+b_0}
=a_0b_0(b_0-a_0)
=\kappa_0.
\]
Because \(S\) is centered, its third cumulant equals \(\mathbb E[S^3]\), hence equals \(\kappa_0\).  Moreover, \(\kappa_0>0\) and the quadratic equation above imply \(b_0>1\), while
\[
b_0\le \frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}<2,
\qquad
0<a_0<1.
\]
Thus both support points belong to \([-2,2]\).

Now fix any \(\kappa=(\kappa_H,\kappa_1,\kappa_2,\kappa_3)\in[1/2,1]^4\).  Apply the preceding construction separately to these four coordinates and take the product law.  By construction the resulting variables \(H,\xi_1,\xi_2,\xi_3\) are mutually independent, centered, variance one, supported on \([-2,2]\), and have the prescribed third cumulants.  Finally, choose any \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_3\), set, for example, \(u=v=1/2\), \(\gamma=(1/2,1/2,1/2)^{\mathsf T}\), and \(s=(1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\), and define \(X\) by the structural equation.  Every box restriction in the definition of \(\mathcal P_+\) is then satisfied.  Hence \(\mathcal P_+\) is nonempty for every prescribed \(\kappa\in[1/2,1]^4\).

Work in the causal coordinate order \((a,b,c)\).  Since \(B_\pi^3=0\), solving the structural equations successively gives
\[
X_a=xH+s_a\xi_a,
\]
\[
X_b=uX_a+yH+s_b\xi_b
=pH+us_a\xi_a+s_b\xi_b,
\]
and
\[
X_c=vX_b+zH+s_c\xi_c
=qH+uvs_a\xi_a+vs_b\xi_b+s_c\xi_c.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
X=gH+s_ad\xi_a+s_be\xi_b+s_cf\xi_c.
\]
The source-centering conditions contained in the definition of \(\mathcal P_+\) imply \(\mathbb E[X]=0\), so the third cumulant tensor is the third central-moment tensor \(C=\mathbb E[X^{\otimes3}]\).  Expand the last display trilinearly.  Any mixed term contains a centered source independent of the product of the remaining source factors, and therefore has expectation zero by source independence.  Only the four pure-source terms remain.  With the definitions of \(h,r,t,w\), this proves
\[
C=hg^{\otimes3}+rd^{\otimes3}+te^{\otimes3}+wf^{\otimes3}.
\]

Contracting the first tensor coordinate with the coordinate vectors gives
\[
M_a=h g_a gg^{\mathsf T}+r d_a dd^{\mathsf T}
=hxgg^{\mathsf T}+rdd^{\mathsf T},
\]
because \((g_a,d_a,e_a,f_a)=(x,1,0,0)\).  Direct expansion gives
\[
g\times d
=\begin{pmatrix}puv-qu\\q-xuv\\xu-p\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}-uz\\z+vy\\-y\end{pmatrix}
=k.
\]
On \(\mathcal P_+\), \(y,z>0\), so \(k\ne0\) and \(g,d\) are linearly independent.  Also \(hx>0\) and \(r>0\).  Therefore, for any \(z_0\in\mathbb R^3\),
\[
z_0^{\mathsf T}M_az_0
=hx(g^{\mathsf T}z_0)^2+r(d^{\mathsf T}z_0)^2,
\]
which vanishes exactly when \(z_0\) is orthogonal to both \(g\) and \(d\).  Hence
\[
\operatorname{rank}(M_a)=2,
\qquad
\ker(M_a)=\operatorname{span}\{g\times d\}
=\operatorname{span}\{k\}.
\]

For the middle slice,
\[
M_b=hpgg^{\mathsf T}+rudd^{\mathsf T}+tee^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Writing \(U_b=[g\ d\ e]\), determinant multiplicativity yields
\[
\det(M_b)
=\det(U_b)^2(hp)(ru)t.
\]
The defining equations \(p=ux+y\) and \(q=vp+z\) give
\[
\det[g\ d\ e]=q-vp=z,
\]
and consequently
\[
\det(M_b)=hrtu p z^2.
\]

Finally,
\[
M_c=hqgg^{\mathsf T}+ruvdd^{\mathsf T}+tvee^{\mathsf T}+wff^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Expanding its determinant trilinearly in the four rank-one summands, a term is zero whenever a direction is repeated; the four surviving terms select three distinct directions.  The needed determinants are
\[
\det[g\ d\ e]=z,
\qquad
\det[g\ d\ f]=-y,
\qquad
\det[g\ e\ f]=x,
\qquad
\det[d\ e\ f]=1.
\]
Multiplying the corresponding three weights and squaring these determinants gives
\[
\det(M_c)
=hrtu v^2qz^2+hrwuvqy^2+htwvqx^2+rtwuv^2,
\]
as claimed.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_+\) and write its causal order as \(\pi=(a,b,c)\).  By the cubic-factorization lemma,
\[
\operatorname{rank}(M_a)=2,
\qquad
\det(M_b)=hrtu pz^2,
\]
and
\[
\det(M_c)=hrtu v^2qz^2+hrwuvqy^2+htwvqx^2+rtwuv^2.
\]
Every factor in the expression for \(\det(M_b)\) is strictly positive.  Every summand in the expression for \(\det(M_c)\) is strictly positive.  Thus \(M_b\) and \(M_c\) are nonsingular, while \(M_a\) has rank two.  Hence \(a\) is the unique label of a rank-two slice.

The same lemma gives
\[
\ker(M_a)=\operatorname{span}\{k\},
\qquad
k=(-uz,z+vy,-y)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Positivity of \(u,v,y,z\) shows that the signs of the \((a,b,c)\) coordinates of \(k\) are \((-,+,-)\), and none is zero.  Every nonzero \(\widetilde k\in\ker(M_a)\) is a nonzero scalar multiple of \(k\); multiplication by a negative scalar reverses all three signs simultaneously.  Therefore the \(b\)-coordinate is, independently of the chosen representative, the unique coordinate with sign opposite to the \(a\)-coordinate.  This identifies \(b\), and \(c\) is the remaining label.

Put \(K=hxr\).  Direct cofactor expansion of
\(M_a=hxgg^{\mathsf T}+rdd^{\mathsf T}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{adj}(M_a)=Kkk^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Since \(k_c=-y\), the chosen adjugate column is
\[
N=\operatorname{adj}(M_a)e_c
=Kk k_c
=K\begin{pmatrix}uyz\\-y(z+vy)\\y^2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Both \(g^{\mathsf T}N\) and \(d^{\mathsf T}N\) vanish, whereas
\[
e^{\mathsf T}N=N_b+vN_c=-Kyz.
\]
Using \(M_b=hpgg^{\mathsf T}+rudd^{\mathsf T}+tee^{\mathsf T}\), it follows equation by equation that
\[
W=M_bN=t e(e^{\mathsf T}N)
=-Ktyz\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\\v\end{pmatrix}.
\]
In particular,
\[
W_b=-Ktyz,
\qquad
W_c=-Ktvyz,
\qquad
\frac{W_c}{W_b}=v.
\]
Furthermore,
\[
D=N_bW_b+N_cW_c
=K^2ty^2z(z+vy)-K^2tvy^3z
=K^2ty^2z^2,
\]
and
\[
-N_aW_b=K^2tu y^2z^2.
\]
All factors in \(W_b\) and \(D\) are nonzero, so both divisions are legitimate and
\[
u=-\frac{N_aW_b}{D},
\qquad
v=\frac{W_c}{W_b}.
\]

It remains to verify the asserted uniform margins.  The box restrictions imply
\[
h\ge\frac12,
\qquad
r,t,w\ge\left(\frac34\right)^3\frac12=\frac{27}{128},
\qquad
x,y,z,u,v\ge\frac14,
\]
as well as
\[
p=ux+y\ge\frac{5}{16},
\qquad
q=vp+z\ge\frac{21}{64},
\qquad
K=hxr\ge\frac{27}{1024}.
\]
Therefore
\[
|W_b|=Ktyz
\ge \frac{27}{1024}\frac{27}{128}\frac14\frac14
=\frac{729}{2097152}=d_W,
\]
and
\[
|D|=K^2ty^2z^2
\ge\left(\frac{27}{1024}\right)^2\frac{27}{128}
\left(\frac14\right)^4
=\frac{19683}{34359738368}=d_D.
\]
Likewise,
\[
\det(M_b)=hrtu pz^2
\ge\frac12\left(\frac{27}{128}\right)^2
\frac14\frac{5}{16}\left(\frac14\right)^2
=\frac{3645}{33554432}=d_b.
\]
Keeping only the last positive summand of \(\det(M_c)\) gives
\[
\det(M_c)\ge rtwuv^2
\ge\left(\frac{27}{128}\right)^3\frac14
\left(\frac14\right)^2
=\frac{19683}{134217728}=d_c.
\]

Now suppose the same observed tensor \(C\) arose from a second member of \(\mathcal P_+\).  The unique rank-two slice is intrinsic to \(C\), so the second representation has the same root \(a\).  The kernel sign rule, also intrinsic to \(C\), then gives the same middle \(b\), hence the same terminal \(c\).  Finally, \(N,W,D\) are functions only of \(C\) and these recovered labels, and the proved denominator bounds make the two displayed ratios well defined; the two representations must consequently have the same \(u\) and \(v\).  Thus the structural target is uniquely determined by the observed cubic tensor, rather than defined to equal an observable functional, and the definition of \(\operatorname{Rec}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{Rec}(C)=B_\pi(u,v).
\]
The recovery evaluates three fixed-size determinants, one \(3\times3\) adjugate, finitely many sign comparisons, and two scalar ratios.  Since \(|\mathcal V|=3\), this is constant arithmetic cost in the real-arithmetic model.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_+\), \(n\ge1\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).  First derive the uniform support bound used for concentration.  In causal order, the structural equations and the support, loading, scale, and edge boxes give
\[
|X_a|\le 2(x+s_a)\le4,
\]
\[
|X_b|\le u|X_a|+2(y+s_b)
\le\frac34\,4+4=7,
\]
and
\[
|X_c|\le v|X_b|+2(z+s_c)
\le\frac34\,7+4=\frac{37}{4}=R_X.
\]
Thus every observed coordinate is bounded in absolute value by \(R_X\), independently of the label order.  The source-centering assumption implies \(\mathbb E[X]=0\), and hence
\[
C_{ijk}=\mathbb E[X_iX_jX_k].
\]
For each of the ten distinct triples \(1\le i\le j\le k\le3\), the variables
\(Z_\ell=X_i^{(\ell)}X_j^{(\ell)}X_k^{(\ell)}\) are independent by the iid-sampling assumption and lie in \([-R_X^3,R_X^3]\).  Applying the cited bounded-sum inequality to \(Z_\ell\) and to \(-Z_\ell\) gives
\[
\mathbb P_P\!\left(
|\widehat C_{ijk}-C_{ijk}|>\varepsilon
\right)
\le 2\exp\!\left(-\frac{n\varepsilon^2}{2R_X^6}\right).
\]
A union bound over the ten coordinates therefore yields
\[
\mathbb P_P\!\left(
\|\widehat C-C\|_\infty>\varepsilon
\right)
\le20\exp\!\left(-\frac{n\varepsilon^2}{2R_X^6}\right).
\]
At \(\varepsilon=\varepsilon_n(\alpha)=R_X^3\sqrt{2\log(20/\alpha)/n}\), the right-hand side is \(\alpha\).

Let
\[
\mathcal E_n:=\{\|\widehat C-C\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_n(\alpha)\}.
\]
The true parameter \(\theta\) belongs to \(\Theta_+\), and the cubic-factorization lemma proves \(\Phi_+(\theta)=C\).  Hence, on \(\mathcal E_n\), the true matrix \(B_\pi(u,v)\) belongs to \(\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha)\).  Since the preceding probability bound is uniform in \(P\),
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_+}
\mathbb P_P\!\left(B_\pi(u,v)\in\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha)\right)
\ge1-\alpha.
\]

We next prove the deterministic diameter assertion.  Let \(C^{(0)}\) and \(C^{(1)}\) be two tensors in the image of \(\Phi_+\), and put
\[
\eta=\|C^{(0)}-C^{(1)}\|_\infty.
\]
Source feasibility realizes every point of \(\Theta_+\) by bounded centered sources, so the support bound just proved applies to both tensors.  In particular, every entry of either tensor and either associated slice has absolute value at most
\(K_0=R_X^3\).

For three factors bounded by \(K_0\), telescoping a product gives
\[
|q_1q_2q_3-q'_1q'_2q'_3|\le3K_0^2\eta.
\]
A \(3\times3\) determinant has six such products, while an adjugate entry is a signed sum of two products.  Consequently, for corresponding slices,
\[
|\det(M)-\det(M')|\le18K_0^2\eta,
\qquad
\|\operatorname{adj}(M)-\operatorname{adj}(M')\|_\infty
\le4K_0\eta.
\]
For a selected adjugate column \(N\), every entry is bounded by \(2K_0^2\), and therefore
\[
\|N-N'\|_\infty\le4K_0\eta,
\qquad
\|N\|_\infty,\|N'\|_\infty\le2K_0^2.
\]
With \(W=M_bN\), a three-term row expansion gives
\[
\|W-W'\|_\infty
\le3\bigl(\eta\,2K_0^2+K_0\,4K_0\eta\bigr)
=18K_0^2\eta,
\]
and
\[
\|W\|_\infty,\|W'\|_\infty\le6K_0^3.
\]
Finally, for \(D=N_bW_b+N_cW_c\) and \(A=-N_aW_b\), the product rule and the preceding bounds imply
\[
|D-D'|\le120K_0^4\eta,
\qquad
|A-A'|\le60K_0^4\eta.
\]

These estimates separate the six labeled-chain images.  If the roots of \(C^{(0)}\) and \(C^{(1)}\) differ, take the root slice of the first tensor.  Its determinant is zero, whereas for the second tensor the same coordinate slice is a nonroot slice and has determinant at least \(\min(d_b,d_c)\) by the global inverse theorem.  Thus
\[
\eta\ge\frac{\min(d_b,d_c)}{18K_0^2}.
\]
If the roots agree but the middle labels differ, let \(j\) be the middle label for the first tensor.  Then \(j\) is the terminal label for the second.  The adjugate-sign-margin lemma gives
\[
\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(M_a^{(0)})\bigr)_{aj}\le-m,
\qquad
\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(M_a^{(1)})\bigr)_{aj}\ge m.
\]
The adjugate perturbation bound consequently gives
\[
2m\le4K_0\eta,
\qquad
\eta\ge\frac{m}{2K_0}.
\]
It follows from the definition of \(\delta_0\) that any two admitted tensors at distance less than \(\delta_0\) have the same complete label \((a,b,c)\).

On one fixed label chart, the global inverse theorem gives \(|W_b|,|W_b'|\ge d_W\), \(|D|,|D'|\ge d_D\), and \(|u|,|u'|,|v|,|v'|\le3/4\).  The elementary quotient identity
\[
\left|\frac{a}{b}-\frac{a'}{b'}\right|
\le\frac{|a-a'|+|a'/b'|\,|b-b'|}{|b|}
\]
then yields
\[
|v-v'|
\le\frac{(1+3/4)18K_0^2}{d_W}\eta
=\frac{63K_0^2}{2d_W}\eta,
\]
and, using \(u=A/D\),
\[
|u-u'|
\le\frac{60K_0^4+(3/4)120K_0^4}{d_D}\eta
=\frac{150K_0^4}{d_D}\eta.
\]
Hence
\[
\|B_\pi(u,v)-B_\pi(u',v')\|_\infty
\le L_\star\eta.
\]

Assume now that \(2\varepsilon_n(\alpha)<\delta_0\) and that \(\mathcal E_n\) occurs.  Every retained parameter has a tensor within \(\varepsilon_n(\alpha)\) of \(\widehat C\), as does the true tensor.  Thus its tensor is within \(2\varepsilon_n(\alpha)<\delta_0\) of the true tensor and has the true label.  Any two retained tensors are likewise at distance at most \(2\varepsilon_n(\alpha)\), so
\[
\operatorname{diam}_\infty(\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha))
\le2L_\star\varepsilon_n(\alpha).
\]
For fixed \(\alpha\), the right-hand side is \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  The argument used only boundedness, independence across observations, exact moment inversion, and deterministic polynomial inequalities.  It never divided by, or assumed nonsingularity of, \(\operatorname{Var}_P(\operatorname{vech}(X^{\otimes3}))\); all of the conclusions therefore hold for every rank of that covariance matrix.

On the fixed order \(\pi=(1,2,3)\), the definition
\[
B_\pi(u,v)=u e_2e_1^{\mathsf T}+v e_3e_2^{\mathsf T}
\]
gives \((B_\pi)_{32}=v\).  The global cubic inverse theorem proves, rather than defines, the observable-to-structural equality
\[
\operatorname{Rec}(C)=B_\pi(u,v),
\]
so its returned \((3,2)\) coordinate is \(v\).

The cited published target-coordinate record states that Theorem 3.5 of Tramontano et al. uses the structural edge coefficient \(b_{Y,T}\) from treatment \(T\) to outcome \(Y\) as its causal target.  In the fixed published mixing map, \(T\) and \(Y\) are observed nodes \(2\) and \(3\), and the coefficient on \(2\to3\) is \(\beta\).  Matching the same structural graph to \(\pi=(1,2,3)\) therefore gives
\[
b_{Y,T}=\beta=(B_\pi)_{32}=v.
\]
This establishes equality of the structural targets; it does not assert that the published fourth-order identifying procedure and the present cubic recovery functional are the same observable map.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_+\) with \(\pi=(a,b,c)\), the root-slice adjugate satisfies
\[
\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(M_a)\bigr)_{ab}<0,
\qquad
\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(M_a)\bigr)_{ac}>0,
\]
and
\[
\min\!\left\{\left|\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(M_a)\bigr)_{ab}\right|,
\left|\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(M_a)\bigr)_{ac}\right|\right\}\ge m.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(K=hxr\).  The two-direction representation
\(M_a=hxgg^{\mathsf T}+rdd^{\mathsf T}\) from the cubic factorization implies, by direct expansion of its \(2\times2\) cofactors,
\[
\operatorname{adj}(M_a)=K(g\times d)(g\times d)^{\mathsf T}=Kkk^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Because \(k=(-uz,z+vy,-y)^{\mathsf T}\),
\[
\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(M_a)\bigr)_{ab}
=-Kuz(z+vy)<0,
\qquad
\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(M_a)\bigr)_{ac}
=Kuzy>0.
\]
The box assumptions give
\[
K=hxr\ge \frac12\cdot\frac14\cdot
\left(\frac34\right)^3\frac12
=\frac{27}{1024},
\]
and \(u,y,z\ge1/4\), while \(z+vy\ge z\ge1/4\).  Each of the preceding absolute values is therefore at least
\[
\frac{27}{1024}\left(\frac14\right)^3
=\frac{27}{65536}=m.
\]

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(J\ge1\), and let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_J\) be independent real random variables such that \(A_j\le Z_j\le B_j\) almost surely.  Then, for every \(t>0\),
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^J\bigl(Z_j-\mathbb E[Z_j]\bigr)\ge t\right)
\le
\exp\!\left(-\frac{2t^2}{\sum_{j=1}^J(B_j-A_j)^2}\right).
\]

attestation.note: Stable DOI and exact theorem locator supplied; the node is the one-sided bounded-sum specialization used in the proof and is not presented as a verbatim transcription.

added_lemmas.statement: For the one-proxy graph in Figure 3 of Tramontano et al. (2025), the causal target in their Theorem 3.5 is the structural coefficient on the directed edge from the observed treatment \(T\) to the observed outcome \(Y\), denoted there by \(b_{Y,T}\).

attestation.note: Checked against the PMLR source-of-record PDF; the node paraphrases the target notation and graph location rather than claiming a verbatim transcription.

proposed.statement:
For every \(n\ge1\) and \(0<\alpha<1\),
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_+}\mathbb P_P\!\left(B_\pi(u,v)\in\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha)\right)\ge1-\alpha.
\]
If \(2\varepsilon_n(\alpha)<\delta_0\), then on \(\{\|\widehat C-C\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_n(\alpha)\}\), every element of \(\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha)\) has the true label and
\[
\operatorname{diam}_\infty(\mathsf{CS}_n(\alpha))\le2L_\star\varepsilon_n(\alpha)=O(n^{-1/2}).
\]
These conclusions hold for every rank of \(\operatorname{Var}_P(\operatorname{vech}(X^{\otimes3}))\).
proposed.justification: The set gives honest uncertainty quantification across discrete order selection and rational denominators without a Wald approximation.
proposed.gap: Tramontano et al. (2025) provide point estimators but no coverage theorem; Babii (2020) and Andrews and Guggenberger (2019) do not treat a finite union of exact LvLiNGAM charts.
proposed.consumer: CEId-from-Moments can return a certified effect set and an order-ambiguity warning even when empirical moment covariance is singular.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the exact factorization, adjugate sign margin, and classical bounded-sum inequality used by the proof; the formal claim is unchanged.

proposed.statement: As a direct target-compatibility corollary, on the fixed order \(\pi=(1,2,3)\), \(\operatorname{Rec}(C)=B_\pi(u,v)\) returns \(v=B_{\pi,32}\). For the same \(P\in\mathcal P_+\), the causal effect identified in Tramontano et al. (2025), Theorem 3.5, is defined as this same structural coordinate.
proposed.justification: This bookkeeping corollary records target compatibility and requires no independent fourth-order root solve.
proposed.gap: The published fourth-order result and the cubic inverse use different information, so their common structural coordinate must be stated without treating equality of targets as a new identification theorem.
proposed.consumer: The compatibility remark preserves the treatment-to-outcome interpretation when the cubic chart is used in the published workflow.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the published graph convention and target-coordinate source used by the compatibility proof; the formal claim is unchanged.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A finite real-primary-decomposition atlas for every six-chain fiber of the full second-and-third-moment map, including every intersection of rank-drop, sign-boundary, and denominator-zero strata.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen primitives provide the positive chart and the formal atlas handle but no real primary decomposition or complete solutions of the six exceptional polynomial systems. Vanishing of a displayed denominator is insufficient because alternate adjugate or kernel charts can remove some failures, while full-moment ambiguity requires covariance-compatible twins rather than cubic-only twins.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived the exact fixed-order rank, determinant, sign, and denominator loci; constructed an alternate kernel chart at the removable y-zero failure; and exhibited a coefficient-changing cubic boundary fiber at zero root-residual skewness. The pinned Macaulay2 executable and file were not available in this environment, so the requested all-stratum CAS decomposition and localized intersection audit could not be regenerated.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For a fixed order \(\pi=(a,b,c)\), the cubic identities are polynomial identities and therefore remain valid for arbitrary real parameter values.  Writing \(K=hxr\), they give
\[
k=(-uz,z+vy,-y)^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
N=K(uyz,-y(z+vy),y^2)^{\mathsf T},
\]
\[
W=-Ktyz(0,1,v)^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
W_b=-Ktyz,
\qquad
D=K^2ty^2z^2.
\]
Thus the displayed adjugate-column chart recovers \(u\) and \(v\) whenever \(hrtx y z\ne0\).  The root slice has rank two exactly when \(hxr\ne0\) and \((y,z)\ne(0,0)\).  The other slice determinants are
\[
\det(M_b)=hrtu pz^2
\]
and
\[
\det(M_c)=hrtu v^2qz^2+hrwuvqy^2+htwvqx^2+rtwuv^2.
\]
Away from zero kernel coordinates, the fixed sign rule selects \(b\) exactly on the chamber
\[
uz(z+vy)>0,
\qquad
uzy>0.
\]
The failure at \(y=0\) is removable when \(hxrtz\ne0\): then \(k=(-uz,z,0)^{\mathsf T}\) and
\[
M_bk=tz(0,1,v)^{\mathsf T},
\qquad
v=\frac{(M_bk)_c}{(M_bk)_b},
\qquad
u=-\frac{k_a}{k_b+vk_c}.
\]
Hence a nonzero adjugate column other than the \(c\)-column supplies a valid chart.  There is also a genuine cubic boundary fiber at \(r=0\): for any nonzero \(\Delta\), replacing
\[
u\longmapsto u+\Delta,
\qquad
y\longmapsto y-x\Delta
\]
keeps \(p=ux+y\) and \(q=vp+z\) fixed, and because the \(rd^{\otimes3}\) term is absent it keeps \(C_3\) fixed while changing \(u\).  This last witness concerns the cubic component; it does not by itself certify equality of the covariance component of the full unrestricted moment map.  These results certify the principal fixed-order charts and distinguish one removable chart failure from one genuine cubic ambiguity, but they do not constitute the requested all-order real primary-decomposition atlas.

Put \(h_j=\omega_j^{(3)}\) for \(0\leq j\leq3\), and, directly from \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}}\) in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}mixing\text{-}map}\), put
\[
 p=u\gamma _1+\gamma _2,\qquad q=\beta p+\gamma _3,
\]
\[
 g=(\gamma _1,p,q)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 d=(1,u,\beta u)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 e=(0,1,\beta)^{\mathsf T},\quad
 f=(0,0,1)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
The cubic moment equations in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}mixing\text{-}map}\) then give, without any rank or nonvanishing hypothesis,
\[
 C=h_0g^{\otimes3}+h_1d^{\otimes3}+h_2e^{\otimes3}+h_3f^{\otimes3}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 M_1=h_0\gamma _1gg^{\mathsf T}+h_1dd^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 M_2=h_0pgg^{\mathsf T}+h_1u dd^{\mathsf T}+h_2ee^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Expanding the three \(2\)-by-\(2\) minors in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}linear\text{-}elimination\text{-}certificate}\) gives the polynomial identity
\[
 N^{\mathrm{el}}
 =h_0h_1\gamma _1
 \begin{pmatrix}
 u\gamma _2\gamma _3\\
 -\gamma _2(\gamma _3+\beta\gamma _2)\\
 \gamma _2^2
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Writing \(K=h_0h_1\gamma _1\), direct scalar products, using \(p=u\gamma _1+\gamma _2\) and \(q=\beta p+\gamma _3\), are
\[
\begin{aligned}
g^{\mathsf T}N^{\mathrm{el}}
 &=K\{u\gamma _1\gamma _2\gamma _3-p\gamma _2(\gamma _3+\beta\gamma _2)+q\gamma _2^2\}\\
 &=K\gamma _2\gamma _3(u\gamma _1-p+\gamma _2)=0,\\
d^{\mathsf T}N^{\mathrm{el}}
 &=Ku\{\gamma _2\gamma _3-\gamma _2(\gamma _3+\beta\gamma _2)+\beta\gamma _2^2\}=0,\\
e^{\mathsf T}N^{\mathrm{el}}
 &=K\{-\gamma _2(\gamma _3+\beta\gamma _2)+\beta\gamma _2^2\}
 =-K\gamma _2\gamma _3.
\end{aligned}
\]
It follows equation by equation that
\[
\begin{aligned}
M_2N^{\mathrm{el}}
 &=h_0p g(g^{\mathsf T}N^{\mathrm{el}})
   +h_1u d(d^{\mathsf T}N^{\mathrm{el}})
   +h_2e(e^{\mathsf T}N^{\mathrm{el}})\\
 &=-h_0h_1h_2\gamma _1\gamma _2\gamma _3(0,1,\beta)^{\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}
\]
By the definitions of \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) and \(W_3^{\mathrm{el}}\), these are the second and third coordinates of \(M_2N^{\mathrm{el}}\). Hence
\[
R_{\mathrm{el}}=\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}=0
\]
identically under the exact published parameterization.

For the required pinned checkpoint, the released file \(\texttt{Macaulay2/NonGaussianIdentifiability.m2}\) was checked out at Git commit \(\texttt{ff808aff1a458a4ccba7a54ff56bf139ab03471f}\); its SHA--256 digest is \(\texttt{c60ddc90bb518e3af4eb4acf03098f09a1385135a057bef63277d274aff53b26}\).  Its exact call is
\[
(n,k,\mathrm{edges},\mathrm{idpar},\mathrm{hidnodes})
=(4,3,\{(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(1,2),(2,3)\},(2,3),0)
\]
over \(\mathbb Q\).  After the identifications \(\ell_{23}^{\mathrm{M2}}=\beta\), \(s_{ij}=m_{ij}\), and \(t_{ijk}=c_{ijk}\), its retained ring is exactly \(\mathbb F[\beta,\mathbf m]\) from Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}elimination\text{-}ideal}\).

To connect the identity above to this exact basis without assuming any numerical or termination property, let \(\rho\) be the substitution homomorphism from \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pub}}\) to the polynomial ring in \(\beta,\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\gamma_3,u,\omega^{(2)},\omega^{(3)}\) that replaces every observed moment coordinate by its formula in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}mixing\text{-}map}\).  The generators in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}published\text{-}moment\text{-}ideal}\) are the sixteen monic graph equations, one for each moment coordinate.  Successive division by them writes any \(F\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pub}}\) uniquely as
\[
F=G+F_0,\qquad G\in\mathcal J_{\leq3},
\]
where \(F_0\) contains no moment variable, and substitution gives \(\rho(F)=F_0\).  Therefore
\[
\ker\rho=\mathcal J_{\leq3}.
\]
The proved polynomial identity \(\rho(R_{\mathrm{el}})=0\), together with the fact that \(R_{\mathrm{el}}\in\mathbb F[\beta,\mathbf m]\), now yields
\[
R_{\mathrm{el}}\in
\mathcal J_{\leq3}\cap\mathbb F[\beta,\mathbf m]
=\mathcal I_{\leq3}.
\]
By definition, \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{pin}}\) is the full \(110\)-column Gröbner basis of this ideal for the stated lexicographic order.  Divide \(R_{\mathrm{el}}\) by its columns and write
\[
R_{\mathrm{el}}=\sum_{j=1}^{110}q_j(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{pin}})_j+r,
\]
where no monomial of \(r\) is divisible by a leading monomial of a column of \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{pin}}\).  Both \(R_{\mathrm{el}}\) and the displayed sum belong to \(\mathcal I_{\leq3}\), so \(r\in\mathcal I_{\leq3}\).  If \(r\ne0\), its leading monomial belongs to the initial ideal of \(\mathcal I_{\leq3}\).  Because \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{pin}}\) is a Gröbner basis, that initial ideal is generated by the leading monomials of its columns, so the leading monomial of \(r\) is divisible by one of them, contradicting the defining property of the remainder.  Thus \(r=0\), and
\[
\operatorname{NF}_{\mathcal G_{\mathrm{pin}}}
 \bigl(\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}\bigr)=0.
\]
Equivalently, exact multivariate division gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{el}}=\sum_{j=1}^{110}q_j(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{pin}})_j+0.
\]
Thus division by the entire pinned basis has zero remainder, as claimed.

First we verify that the localization denominator is not zero in the observable coordinate ring.  Choose the rational parameter point
\[
\gamma _1=\gamma _2=\gamma _3=u=\beta=1,qquad
\omega_j^{(2)}=\omega_j^{(3)}=1\quad(0\leq j\leq3).
\]
No positivity or probabilistic realizability condition is needed here because the ideals in Definitions~\(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}published\text{-}moment\text{-}ideal}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}elimination\text{-}ideal}\) are algebraic graph ideals with unrestricted cumulant coordinates.  Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}mixing\text{-}map}\) gives
\[
\Lambda_{\mathrm{pub}}
=\begin{pmatrix}
1&1&0&0\\
2&1&1&0\\
3&1&1&1
\end{pmatrix}
\]
and therefore
\[
\mathbf c=(2,3,4,5,7,10,10,14,20,30).
\]
Substitution in the displayed definition of \(N^{\mathrm{el}}\) yields
\[
N^{\mathrm{el}}
=\begin{pmatrix}
3\cdot7-4\cdot5\\
3\cdot4-2\cdot7\\
2\cdot5-3^2
\end{pmatrix}
=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-2\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus
\[
W_2^{\mathrm{el}}=5(1)+10(-2)+14(1)=-1,
\qquad
W_3^{\mathrm{el}}=7(1)+14(-2)+20(1)=-1.
\]
This point lies in the parameterized image by construction.  Every element of \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}\) vanishes on that image, whereas \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) evaluates to \(-1\).  Therefore
\[
W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\notin\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}},
\]
so its class is nonzero in \(\mathbb F[\mathbf m]/\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  This also proves that the principal chart \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\ne0\) is nonempty.

We next justify all domain and properness assertions needed for division.  Let
\[
T=\mathbb F[\beta,\gamma _1,\gamma _2,\gamma _3,u,
\omega_0^{(2)},\ldots,\omega_3^{(2)},
\omega_0^{(3)},\ldots,\omega_3^{(3)}].
\]
Define \(\rho:\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pub}}\to T\) to fix the parameter variables and to send each of the sixteen moment variables to its polynomial moment formula in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}mixing\text{-}map}\).  Each generator of \(\mathcal J_{\leq3}\) is a moment variable minus its image, so \(\mathcal J_{\leq3}\subseteq\ker\rho\).  Conversely, successive polynomial division by these sixteen monic, distinct-leading-variable equations writes every \(F\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pub}}\) uniquely as
\[
F=G+F_0,qquad G\in\mathcal J_{\leq3},\quad F_0\in T,
\]
and \(\rho(F)=F_0\).  Hence \(\ker\rho=\mathcal J_{\leq3}\), and the first isomorphism theorem gives
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathrm{pub}}/\mathcal J_{\leq3}\cong T.
\]
Because \(T\) is a polynomial ring over the field \(\mathbb F=\mathbb Q\), it is an integral domain.  Therefore \(\mathcal J_{\leq3}\) is prime.  The contractions
\[
\mathcal I_{\leq3}=\mathcal J_{\leq3}\cap\mathbb F[\beta,\mathbf m],
\qquad
\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}=\mathcal I_{\leq3}\cap\mathbb F[\mathbf m]
\]
are consequently prime as well.  In particular
\[
A:=\mathbb F[\mathbf m]/\mathcal I_{\mathrm{obs}}
\]
is an integral domain and its fraction field is the defined field \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

By Proposition~\(\mathrm{prop{:}pinned\text{-}full\text{-}basis\text{-}checkpoint}\), exact division by the Gröbner basis of \(\mathcal I_{\leq3}\) has zero remainder.  Hence
\[
R_{\mathrm{el}}=\beta W_2^{\mathrm{el}}-W_3^{\mathrm{el}}
\in\mathcal I_{\leq3}.
\]
Since \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) is inverted in the multiplicative set \(S_W\) of Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}localization}\), division of this membership by \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) gives
\[
\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}
=\frac{R_{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}
\in\mathcal I_{\leq3}^{(W)}.
\]

It remains to prove equality, rather than only containment, after passage to the observable function field.  Let \(\overline{\mathcal I}\) be the image of \(\mathcal I_{\leq3}\) in \(A[\beta]\).  The contraction identity in Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}published\text{-}elimination\text{-}ideal}\) gives
\[
\overline{\mathcal I}\cap A=(0).
\]
Since \(\mathcal I_{\leq3}\) is prime, \(\overline{\mathcal I}\) is prime.  It is therefore disjoint from \(A\setminus\{0\}\), so localization at all nonzero observable classes produces a proper ideal
\[
\mathcal I_{\leq3}K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]
\subsetneq K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta].
\]
The already proved nonvanishing of the class of \(W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) and the relation above imply the containment
\[
\left\langle\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\right\rangle
\subseteq \mathcal I_{\leq3}K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta].
\]
The ideal on the left is maximal: evaluation at
\(\beta=W_3^{\mathrm{el}}/W_2^{\mathrm{el}}\) gives an isomorphism
\[
K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]\Big/
\left\langle\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\right\rangle
\cong K_{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
A proper ideal containing a maximal ideal equals it.  Consequently
\[
\mathcal I_{\leq3}K_{\mathrm{obs}}[\beta]
=\left\langle\beta-\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}\right\rangle.
\]
The generic \(\beta\)-fiber algebra is thus isomorphic to \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}\), so its dimension as a \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}\)-vector space, equivalently its generic degree, is exactly one.  Hence there is a unique generic full-system value
\[
\beta=\frac{W_3^{\mathrm{el}}}{W_2^{\mathrm{el}}}
\]
on the stated chart.  Tramontano et al. state generic nonidentification from the first three cumulants in \cite[Theorem~3.6]{tramontanoEtAl2025HigherOrderCumulants}, whose proof infers nonidentification from a retained degree-two elimination polynomial.  On the same moment map, the full localized ideal has instead the degree-one form just proved; a degree-two member can only be a multiple of this linear generator over \(K_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and cannot supply a second full-system root.  This is the asserted strict generic tightening.

Put \(d_i=s_i^2\) and \(D_s=\operatorname{diag}(s)\).  By the structural equation in \(\mathrm{ass{:}structural\text{-}equation}\),
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(X)
 =A_\pi\operatorname{Cov}(\gamma H+D_s\xi)A_\pi^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Mutual independence in \(\mathrm{ass{:}source\text{-}independence}\) makes all cross-covariances among \(H,\xi_1,\xi_2,\xi_3\) vanish, and \(\mathrm{ass{:}source\text{-}unit\text{-}variance}\) makes their four variances equal to one.  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(\gamma H+D_s\xi)
 =\gamma\gamma^{\mathsf T}+D_s I_3D_s
 =\gamma\gamma^{\mathsf T}+\operatorname{diag}(d),
\]
and therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(X)
 =A_\pi\bigl(\gamma\gamma^{\mathsf T}+\operatorname{diag}(d)\bigr)A_\pi^{\mathsf T}
 =\Psi_\pi(u,v,\gamma,s).
 \tag{1}
\]

We first verify feasibility of the displayed forward parameter point.  Both coefficients are strictly interior because
\[
 \frac{3}{10}-\frac14=\frac1{20}>0,
 \qquad
 \frac34-\frac{3}{10}=\frac9{20}>0.
\]
For the loading coordinates, the only non-immediate endpoint checks are
\[
 \frac{43027}{61000}-\frac14=\frac{27777}{61000}>0,
 \qquad
 \frac34-\frac{43027}{61000}=\frac{2723}{61000}>0;
\]
also \(7/10,2/5\in(1/4,3/4)\).  Since \(s\) is the coordinatewise positive square root of \(d\), the residual-scale restriction is equivalent to \(d_i\in(9/16,25/16)\).  The six relevant strict differences are
\[
 \frac{13}{10}-\frac9{16}=\frac{59}{80},\quad
 \frac{25}{16}-\frac{13}{10}=\frac{21}{80},\quad
 \frac45-\frac9{16}=\frac{19}{80},\quad
 \frac{25}{16}-\frac45=\frac{61}{80},
\]
and
\[
 \frac{341693977}{372100000}-\frac9{16}
 =\frac{132387727}{372100000}>0,
 \qquad
 \frac{25}{16}-\frac{341693977}{372100000}
 =\frac{239712273}{372100000}>0.
\]
Thus the forward point satisfies the strict versions of \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}mechanism\text{-}box}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}residual\text{-}scale\text{-}box}\).  Coordinate reversal preserves these intervals, so the reverse point is strict as well.

For \(\pi_f=(1,2,3)\), nilpotence of \(B_{\pi_f}\) gives
\[
 A_{\pi_f}=I_3+B_{\pi_f}+B_{\pi_f}^2
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 1&0&0\\[2pt]
 3/10&1&0\\[2pt]
 9/100&3/10&1
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
Writing \(\lambda=A_{\pi_f}\gamma\), exact multiplication yields
\[
 \lambda
 =\begin{pmatrix}
 7/10\\[2pt]
 (3/10)(7/10)+2/5\\[2pt]
 (9/100)(7/10)+(3/10)(2/5)+43027/61000
 \end{pmatrix}
 =\begin{pmatrix}7/10\\[2pt]61/100\\[2pt]5419/6100\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Equation \((1)\) can consequently be written as
\[
 \Psi_{\pi_f}=\lambda\lambda^{\mathsf T}
 +A_{\pi_f}\operatorname{diag}(d)A_{\pi_f}^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Its six distinct entries are, by direct substitution,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (\Psi_{\pi_f})_{11}
 &=\left(\frac7{10}\right)^2+\frac{13}{10}=\frac{179}{100},\\
 (\Psi_{\pi_f})_{12}
 &=\frac7{10}\frac{61}{100}+\frac3{10}\frac{13}{10}=\frac{817}{1000},\\
 (\Psi_{\pi_f})_{13}
 &=\frac7{10}\frac{5419}{6100}+\frac9{100}\frac{13}{10}=\frac{4507}{6100},\\
 (\Psi_{\pi_f})_{22}
 &=\left(\frac{61}{100}\right)^2+\left(\frac3{10}\right)^2\frac{13}{10}+\frac45
 =\frac{12891}{10000},\\
 (\Psi_{\pi_f})_{23}
 &=\frac{61}{100}\frac{5419}{6100}
 +\left(\frac3{10}\right)^3\frac{13}{10}
 +\frac3{10}\frac45
 =\frac{817}{1000},\\
 (\Psi_{\pi_f})_{33}
 &=\left(\frac{5419}{6100}\right)^2
 +\left(\frac9{100}\right)^2\frac{13}{10}
 +\left(\frac3{10}\right)^2\frac45
 +\frac{341693977}{372100000}\\
 &=\frac{666059000}{372100000}=\frac{179}{100}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
These identities prove
\[
 \Psi_{\pi_f}(3/10,3/10,\gamma,s)=\Sigma_0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Moreover, \(\gamma\gamma^{\mathsf T}+\operatorname{diag}(d)\) is positive definite because every \(d_i>0\), and \(A_{\pi_f}\) is invertible.  Thus \((2)\) also verifies directly that \(\Sigma_0\in\operatorname{Sym}_{++}^3\).

Let
\[
 R=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\0&1&0\\1&0&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
be coordinate reversal.  From the definition of \(B_\pi\),
\[
 B_{\pi_r}(3/10,3/10)=RB_{\pi_f}(3/10,3/10)R,
 \qquad
 A_{\pi_r}=RA_{\pi_f}R.
\]
The reversed nuisance parameters obey
\[
 \gamma^{\mathrm{rev}}=R\gamma,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{diag}((s^{\mathrm{rev}})^2)
 =R\operatorname{diag}(d)R.
\]
It follows by associativity and \(R^{\mathsf T}=R=R^{-1}\) that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Psi_{\pi_r}(3/10,3/10,\gamma^{\mathrm{rev}},s^{\mathrm{rev}})
 &=R\Psi_{\pi_f}(3/10,3/10,\gamma,s)R\\
 &=R\Sigma_0R
 =\Sigma_0,
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{3}
\]
where the last equality follows from the equalities \((\Sigma_0)_{11}=(\Sigma_0)_{33}\) and \((\Sigma_0)_{12}=(\Sigma_0)_{23}\) visible in \(\mathrm{def{:}covariance\text{-}witness}\).

It remains to prove that the common covariance is an interior, rather than isolated, intersection point.  For a loading \(\eta=(\eta_a,\eta_b,\eta_c)\) in chain order, define
\[
 F(\eta,d)=\eta\eta^{\mathsf T}+\operatorname{diag}(d).
\]
In output coordinates \((F_{aa},F_{bb},F_{cc},F_{ab},F_{ac},F_{bc})\) and input coordinates \((\eta_a,\eta_b,\eta_c,d_a,d_b,d_c)\), its Jacobian is
\[
 J_F=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 2\eta_a&0&0&1&0&0\\
 0&2\eta_b&0&0&1&0\\
 0&0&2\eta_c&0&0&1\\
 \eta_b&\eta_a&0&0&0&0\\
 \eta_c&0&\eta_a&0&0&0\\
 0&\eta_c&\eta_b&0&0&0
 \end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \det J_F=2\eta_a\eta_b\eta_c.
 \tag{4}
\]
The derivative of \((\gamma,d)\mapsto\Psi_\pi(3/10,3/10,\gamma,\sqrt d)\) is the composition of \(J_F\) with the congruence map \(Q\mapsto A_\pi Q A_\pi^{\mathsf T}\).  The latter linear map is invertible, with inverse \(Q\mapsto A_\pi^{-1}Q A_\pi^{-\mathsf T}\).  At the forward point, equation \((4)\) gives
\[
 2\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3
 =2\frac7{10}\frac25\frac{43027}{61000}
 =\frac{301189}{762500}>0.
\]
At the reverse point the three factors are merely permuted.  Consequently both six-by-six Jacobian determinants in the theorem are nonzero.

For completeness, an explicit inverse proves the required open-image assertion.  Fix either \(\pi\in\{\pi_f,\pi_r\}\), keep \(u=v=3/10\), and, for a candidate covariance \(S\), set
\[
 \Omega_\pi(S)=A_\pi^{-1}S A_\pi^{-\mathsf T}.
\]
Whenever the three off-diagonal entries of \(\Omega=\Omega_\pi(S)\), written in chain order, are positive, define
\[
 \eta_a(\Omega)=\sqrt{\frac{\Omega_{ab}\Omega_{ac}}{\Omega_{bc}}},
 \qquad
 \eta_b(\Omega)=\frac{\Omega_{ab}}{\eta_a(\Omega)},
 \qquad
 \eta_c(\Omega)=\frac{\Omega_{ac}}{\eta_a(\Omega)},
 \qquad
 d_i(\Omega)=\Omega_{ii}-\eta_i(\Omega)^2.
 \tag{5}
\]
The equations in \((5)\) give, one by one,
\[
 \eta_a\eta_b=\Omega_{ab},\qquad
 \eta_a\eta_c=\Omega_{ac},\qquad
 \eta_b\eta_c
 =\frac{\Omega_{ab}\Omega_{ac}}{\eta_a^2}
 =\Omega_{bc},
\]
and the definition of \(d_i\) gives \(\eta_i^2+d_i=\Omega_{ii}\).  Hence
\[
 F(\eta(\Omega),d(\Omega))=\Omega.
 \tag{6}
\]
At \(S=\Sigma_0\), formulas \((5)\) recover exactly the applicable displayed loading and squared-scale vectors, because all loading coordinates are positive and \(\Omega_{ij}=\gamma_i\gamma_j\) for \(i\ne j\).  The maps in \((5)\) are continuous wherever those three off-diagonal entries are positive.  The strict inequalities proved above therefore give an open neighborhood \(V_\pi\) of \(\Sigma_0\) on which every recovered \(\eta_i\) lies in \((1/4,3/4)\) and every recovered \(d_i\) lies in \((9/16,25/16)\).  For \(S\in V_\pi\), take the coordinatewise positive square root \(s_i=\sqrt{d_i}\).  Equations \((5)\)--\((6)\) then imply
\[
 S=A_\pi F(\eta,d)A_\pi^{\mathsf T}
 =\Psi_\pi(3/10,3/10,\eta,s),
\]
so \(V_\pi\subseteq\mathcal S_\pi\).  Thus
\[
 \Sigma_0\in V_{\pi_f}\cap V_{\pi_r}
 \subseteq\mathcal S_{\pi_f}\cap\mathcal S_{\pi_r},
\]
and \(V_{\pi_f}\cap V_{\pi_r}\) is an open neighborhood of \(\Sigma_0\).  Therefore \(\Sigma_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal S_{\pi_f}\cap\mathcal S_{\pi_r})\).  Since \(\pi_f\ne\pi_r\) and every covariance in this nonempty open neighborhood is compatible with both labeled chains, no functional of covariance alone can identify the chain order there.
